title: openalex_W4415110710
universal_lens: Longitudinal Bayesian inference over behavioral regimes under pandemic stress, mapping gaming excess to sleep quality and depression via IGDS9-SF and PSQI scales. Pandemic-induced behavioral shift in adolescent video gaming correlates with mental health outcomes via temporal comparative analysis.
gsi_mapping: GSI models adaptive risk inference using IGDS9-SF and PSQI as conformal predictors for gaming disorder escalation during pandemic phases. Bayesian belief updates on gaming time and symptom severity using pre/post pandemic data distributions with conformal predictive intervals.
gse_mapping: GSE encodes state transitions in adolescent gaming behavior through multi-agent simulation of screen time, exercise, and mental health metrics across pre/post pandemic epochs. State transitions in adolescent behavior modeled through multi-agent simulation: gaming time → sleep quality → depressive symptoms → substance use.

primitives.name: Excessive Gaming Behavior Regime
primitives.verbatim_quote: This study aimed to assess how the COVID-19 pandemic influenced the gaming behaviors of adolescents who engaged in excessive video gaming.
primitives.assumptions: Behavioral patterns are measurable via self-reporting scales; gaming excess is defined as >2 hrs/day.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Pandemic-induced behavioral shift beyond baseline norms.

layer2.mapping: Kernel density estimation of gaming time distribution across pandemic vs. pre-pandemic periods.

primitives.name: Sleep Quality Index Under Stress
primitives.verbatim_quote: Although excessive players scored significantly higher than the control group on the PSQI and IGDS9-SF, no significant difference was observed in CDI scores (p = 0.091).
primitives.assumptions: Sleep quality correlates with gaming excess; mental health outcomes are separable from gaming behavior.
primitives.breakdown_regime: No significant change in depressive symptoms despite increased screen time.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic mapping between PSQI and IGDS9-SF as indicators of behavioral dysregulation.

primitives.name: Pandemic Adaptation Curve
primitives.verbatim_quote: Results: Among excessive video game players, both screen time (p < 0.001) and daily exercise duration (p = 0.001) increased significantly during the pandemic.
primitives.assumptions: Adolescent adaptation to lockdown is reflected in behavioral metrics such as screen time and physical activity.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Behavioral normalization under enforced sedentary constraints.

layer2.mapping: Kernel regression of screen time against exercise duration during pandemic.

primitives.name: Risk Factor Evolution During Crisis
primitives.verbatim_quote: Conclusions: Despite the increase in screen time among excessive players, problematic gaming behaviors did not escalate.
primitives.assumptions: Problematic gaming behavior can be quantified and monitored over time.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Stable risk profile despite environmental stressors.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic representation of risk evolution using IGDS9-SF as proxy for escalation likelihood.
